visual_brief: Aconcagua is a broad, double-summited Andean massif with horizontal rock bands, hanging glaciers, and a huge south wall above dry, brown valleys. Classic views look up the Horcones valley toward its snowy south face, while aerial views reveal its full glaciated bulk and western views show more exposed rock. Avoid confusing nearby Cerro Cuerno, Catedral, or Bonete with Aconcagua itself.
notes: Six distinct JPEGs visually checked; all long sides >=2400 px. c1 is the strongest classic view; c2 offers an aerial alternative. A wrongly tagged neighbouring peak and obscured summit views were discarded. c1-c3 state Unsplash License; remaining sources state no reuse licence.
